s: Which Sri Lankan king was defeated and captured by Rajendra I when he completed the Chola conquest of Ceylon?
x: Rajendra I completed the conquest of Ceylon by taking its southern part and capturing Mahinda V, building on Rajaraja I's conquest of the north.

s: Which Chola ruler conquered the whole of Sri Lanka, defeating Mahinda V and seizing his royal insignia?
x: Rajendra I completed the conquest of Sri Lanka by defeating Mahinda V and seizing the royal insignia; the island stayed under the Cholas for about five decades. Rajaraja I had taken only the north, Rajadhiraja I fell at Koppam, and in Kulottunga I's time Vijayabahu I expelled the Cholas (c. 1070).

s: Where did Rajaraja I destroy the Chera navy?
x: Rajaraja I destroyed the Chera fleet at Kandalur Salai (Trivandrum) and captured Quilon.

s: Which Chola ruler conquered the Maldives islands?
x: Rajaraja I's naval conquests included the Maldives, the Chera fleet and northern Sri Lanka.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Rajaraja I — Kadaram conquest in 1025 CE
x: The 1025 CE Kadaram conquest was conducted by Rajendra I. Rajaraja I is associated with the Maldives and the attack on the Chera fleet at Kandalur Salai, while Kulottunga I campaigned in Kalinga.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Rajendra I – Naval expedition against Kadaram and Srivijaya
Kulottunga I – Defeat of Pallava Aparajita
Aditya I – Loss at Thakkolam to the Rashtrakutas
x: Rajendra I sent the naval expedition to Kadaram and Srivijaya. Aditya I defeated Pallava Aparajita, Parantaka I lost at Thakkolam and Kulottunga I abolished tolls.

s: Against which kingdom was the naval expedition of Rajendra I in 1025 CE directed?
x: Rajendra I's 1025 CE naval expedition was against the revived Srivijaya empire: he defeated the Sailendra king and took Kadaram (Kedah) in Malaya and parts of Sumatra. Anuradhapura was destroyed by Rajaraja I, and Kalinga was conquered by Kulottunga I.

s: Which historian said the Cholas turned the Bay of Bengal into a 'Chola Lake'?
x: K.A. Nilakanta Sastri described the Bay of Bengal as a 'Chola Lake'; the 1025 CE Srivijaya expedition was led by Rajendra I.

s: Chola overseas naval activity helped spread which art tradition to Southeast Asia?
x: The Cholas, described as the first Indian power with overseas naval campaigns, helped spread Dravidian art to Southeast Asia.

s: What was the main cause of the Chola expedition against Srivijaya?
o: blocked Indian traders on the China route
x: Chola-Sailendra ties, once cordial, soured when Srivijaya blocked Indian traders on the China route; Rajendra I's 1025 CE expedition cleared these obstacles and widened Chola trade with China.

s: Who were the first Indian power to carry out overseas naval campaigns?
x: The Imperial Cholas were the first Indian power with overseas naval campaigns, reaching Sri Lanka, the Maldives and Srivijaya.

s: Who expelled the Cholas from Sri Lanka around 1070?
x: Vijayabahu I expelled the Cholas from Sri Lanka around 1070.

s: The Chola hold over Sri Lanka developed in which of the following ways?
o: Kulottunga I first conquered the north, and Rajendra III retained the whole island
Vijayabahu I established Chola rule over the whole island for about five decades
Rajaraja I controlled the whole island, while Rajendra I restricted Chola control to the north
Rajaraja I controlled the north, while Rajendra I extended control to the whole island for about five decades
x: Rajaraja I established Chola control in northern Sri Lanka, and Rajendra I extended it to the whole island, which remained under Chola control for about five decades.

s: Which Chola ruler placed Saktivarman and Vimaladitya as Eastern Chalukya princes in Vengi?
x: Rajaraja I arranged Vengi by placing Saktivarman and Vimaladitya there; he also captured Quilon, annexed Madurai and conquered the Maldives.

s: Whose Kalinga conquest is celebrated in Jayamkondar's Kalingattuparani?
x: Kulottunga I conquered Kalinga, a campaign sung in Jayamkondar's Kalingattuparani.

s: Whom did the Chola princess Madhurantaki marry?
x: Madhurantaki married Rajendra Chalukya, who became Kulottunga I. Kundavai married Vimaladitya, Ammanga Devi married Rajaraja Narendra, and Saktivarman I was Vimaladitya's elder brother who ruled Vengi with Rajaraja I's help.

s: Who married Vimaladitya, according to the Chola–Eastern Chalukya matrimonial alliances?
o: Ammanga Devi, daughter of Rajendra I
x: Kundavai, the daughter of Rajaraja I, married Vimaladitya. Ammanga Devi married Rajaraja Narendra.

s: After whose ouster did Saktivarman I rule Vengi with the help of Rajaraja I?
x: Saktivarman I, the elder brother of Vimaladitya, ruled Vengi with Rajaraja I’s help after Jatachoda Bhima was ousted.

s: Whose daughter was Madhurantaki, the wife of Kulottunga I?
x: Madhurantaki was the daughter of Rajendra II and married Rajendra Chalukya (Kulottunga I).

s: Whom did Ammanga Devi, daughter of Rajendra I, marry?
x: Ammanga Devi married Rajaraja Narendra in 1022. Their son was Rajendra Chalukya, who later became Kulottunga I.

s: Who was the last ruler of the Chalukya-Chola line in Vengi?
x: Parantaka Chola was the last ruler of the Chalukya-Chola line in Vengi. Vijayaditya VII was the last Eastern Chalukya before the merger under Kulottunga I.

s: What did Kulottunga I do after the death of Vijayaditya VII in 1075?
o: merged Vengi with his Chola dominions
abandoned the Chola kingdom and returned to China
transferred the Chola capital to Uraiyur
x: After Vijayaditya VII’s death in 1075, Kulottunga I merged Vengi with his Chola dominions and ruled both regions, giving rise to the Chalukya-Chola association.

s: The Chola viceroy Rajaraja (Mummadi Chola), son of Kulottunga I, installed whom in Kalinga?
x: Rajaraja (Mummadi Chola) installed Anantavarman Chodaganga in Kalinga; Gonka I was his commander.

s: With which place is Jananathapura, where the Chola viceroy Rajaraja Chola Ganga was crowned, identified?
x: Rajaraja Chola Ganga was crowned at Jananathapura (Draksharama); his Tekkali inscription records his rule.

s: Who was the last Eastern Chalukya ruler of Vengi?
x: Vijayaditya VII was the last Eastern Chalukya; Parantaka Chola was the last Chalukya-Chola ruler in Vengi.

s: Which ruler united the Tamil (Chola) and Andhra (Vengi) kingdoms?
x: Kulottunga I united the Tamil and Andhra kingdoms; Vengi had been a prize in the Chola-Chalukya wars, and the Mandalika Yugam followed (1076 to c. 1210).

s: Which period of Andhra history followed the merger of Vengi with the Chola dominions and is known as the Mandalika Yugam?
x: After the Chalukya-Chola merger, the Mandalika Yugam lasted from 1076 to about 1210.

s: The Tekkali inscription belongs to which Chola viceroy of Vengi?
x: Rajaraja Chola Ganga, crowned at Jananathapura (Draksharama), is known from the Tekkali inscription.

s: Who was the commander of Rajaraja (Mummadi Chola), the son of Kulottunga I and viceroy of Vengi?
x: Gonka I was the commander of the viceroy Rajaraja (Mummadi Chola), who ruled from Jagannathapuram.

s: Which of the following factors contributed to the decline of the Chalukya-Cholas after Kulottunga I?
o: Complete withdrawal of the Cholas from Vengi before Kulottunga I
Strengthening of the central bureaucracy and disappearance of local chiefs
Abolition of local authority by the Pandyas
Weakening of the central bureaucracy and growth of local chieftains
x: After Kulottunga I, the central bureaucracy weakened and local chieftains grew in power. The Chalukya-Cholas subsequently declined with the rise of the Pandyas.

s: What did the Chola king Kulottunga I (1070-1122 CE) abolish?
x: Kulottunga I abolished tolls and married his daughter to a Sinhala prince; the Brihadeeswara temple was built by Rajaraja I.

s: Who was the mother of Rajendra Chalukya (Kulottunga I), son of Rajaraja Narendra?
x: Kulottunga I, also called Rajendra Chalukya, was the son of Rajaraja Narendra and Ammanga Devi and took the Chola throne in 1070 CE.

s: How many merchants did Kulottunga I send in his embassy to China?
x: Kulottunga I sent 72 merchants to China as part of the diplomatic and commercial contact recorded for his reign.

s: In which year did Kulottunga I send 72 merchants to China?
x: Kulottunga I sent a goodwill mission of 72 merchants to China in 1077.

s: From which of the following is the name 'Coromandel' derived?
x: 'Coromandel' comes from Cholamandalam, not Tondaimandalam (the former Pallava country); the Chola core was the Kaveri delta.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Imperial Cholas flourished approximately from the 4th to the 6th century CE.
Parantaka I defeated the Pandyas and Sri Lanka.
Rajaraja I ruled from 985 to 1014 CE.
Aditya I defeated the Pallava ruler Aparajita and expanded northward.
x: Option A is incorrect: the Imperial Cholas, founded by Vijayalaya, flourished from about the 9th to the 13th century CE. Parantaka I did fight the Pandyas and Sri Lanka, Rajaraja I ruled 985–1014 CE, and Aditya I defeated Aparajita.

s: Where was Vijayalaya a feudatory of the Pallavas before he founded the imperial Chola line?
x: Vijayalaya was a Pallava feudatory at Uraiyur and captured Thanjavur from the Muttaraiyars in 850 CE.

s: From whom did Vijayalaya capture Thanjavur in 850 CE?
x: Vijayalaya took Thanjavur from the Muttaraiyars in 850 CE and founded the imperial Chola line.

s: Who founded the Imperial Chola dynasty by capturing Tanjavur?
x: Vijayalaya founded the Imperial Chola line in the mid-9th century by taking Thanjavur from the Muttaraiyars. Aditya I, Parantaka I and Rajaraja I were later rulers.

s: Who succeeded Vijayalaya, the founder of the imperial Chola line?
x: Vijayalaya founded the line by taking Thanjavur in 850 CE; his successor was Aditya I, not Parantaka I.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Vijayalaya captured Thanjavur from the Muttaraiyars.
2. Parantaka I was the immediate successor of Vijayalaya.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Vijayalaya took Thanjavur from the Muttaraiyars in 850 CE, but he was succeeded by Aditya I; Parantaka I came after Aditya I.

s: Who among the following was killed at Koppam while mounted on an elephant?
x: Rajadhiraja I was killed at Koppam on the back of an elephant and was known by the title Yanai-mel-thunjina Devar.

s: By what other name was the Chola king Rajaraja I (985-1014 CE) known?
x: Rajaraja I, also known as Arumolivarman, ruled 985-1014 CE and made the Chola state the largest in South India.

s: The Uttaramerur inscriptions are associated with which Chola ruler?
x: The Uttaramerur inscriptions are associated with Parantaka I. He was defeated at Takkolam in 949 CE.

s: Who was the last ruler of the Imperial Chola dynasty?
x: Rajendra III (1246–1279) was the last Imperial Chola; the Pandyas rose after him.

s: Which Chola ruler was crowned on the battlefield of Koppam?
x: Rajendra II was crowned on the field at Koppam after Rajadhiraja I was killed; he set up a victory pillar at Kolhapur.

s: Which statement correctly describes Kulottunga I?
o: He was killed at Koppam while riding an elephant.
He was the founder who captured Thanjavur in 850 CE.
He defeated Pallava Aparajita and annexed Tondaimandalam.
He was the first ruler of the Chalukya-Chola line and ruled from 1070 to 1122 CE.
x: Kulottunga I was the first ruler of the Chalukya-Chola line (1070-1122 CE). Rajadhiraja I died at Koppam, Vijayalaya took Thanjavur, and Aditya I defeated Aparajita and annexed Tondaimandalam.

s:
Arrange the following Chola rulers in chronological order:
1. Rajaraja I
2. Aditya I
3. Vijayalaya
4. Rajendra I
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: The order is Vijayalaya (c. 850) → Aditya I → Rajaraja I (985–1014) → Rajendra I (1014–1044).

s: Where did the Chola king Rajendra II set up a victory pillar?
x: Rajendra II, crowned on the battlefield of Koppam, set up a victory pillar at Kolhapur.

s: Which of the following was the earliest capital associated with the Sangam Cholas?
x: Uraiyur was the early Sangam Chola capital. Thanjavur became important under the Imperial Cholas, while Gangaikondacholapuram was established by Rajendra I.

s: In which year was Gangaikondacholapuram founded as the new Chola capital?
x: Rajendra I founded Gangaikondacholapuram c. 1035 CE; 1010 is the completion of the Brihadeeswara temple.

s: Who among the following is credited with building Rajahmundry (Rajamahendravaram)?
x: Amma I made Rajamahendravaram the capital, but Rajaraja Narendra made it famous and is credited with building it.

s: Under which dynasty was the Brihadeeswara temple at Thanjavur built?
x: The Brihadeeswara (Rajarajeshwara) temple at Thanjavur was built by the Chola king Rajaraja I and completed in 1010 CE.

s: In which year was the Brihadeeswara temple at Thanjavur completed by Rajaraja I?
x: Rajaraja I completed the Brihadeeswara (Rajarajeshwara) temple in 1010 CE.

s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler made Rajamahendravaram his capital?
x: Amma I made Rajamahendravaram the capital; Rajaraja Narendra later made it famous.

s:
Consider the following statements about Rajamahendravaram:
1. Amma I made it his capital.
2. Rajaraja Narendra made it famous.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Amma I made Rajamahendravaram the capital and Rajaraja Narendra made it famous, so both are correct.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Maduraikonda was the title of Parantaka I, not Kulottunga I. Rajaraja I was known as Mummadi Chola, Rajendra I as Gangaikondachola, and Rajadhiraja I as Yanai-mel-thunjina Devar.

s: Which Chola ruler took the title 'Ulakalanda Perumal', reflecting a land survey and revenue reorganisation?
x: Ulakalanda Perumal and Mummudi Chola were titles of Rajaraja I; Madurai-konda was Parantaka I's and Gangaikonda Chola Rajendra I's.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Gangaikonda Chola — Rajendra I's Ganga expedition
Mummudi Chola — Rajendra I's conquest of Kadaram
Pandita Chola — Rajendra I's patronage of learning
Kadaram Kondan — Rajendra I's conquest of Kadaram
x: Mummudi Chola was a title of Rajaraja I, associated with northern Sri Lanka being named Mummadichola Mandalam. Kadaram Kondan, Pandita Chola and Gangaikonda Chola were associated with Rajendra I.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kulottunga I — Kulottunga Cholapuram at Visakhapatnam
x: Vengi Purveshwara was a title assumed by Someshvara I after Koppam. Kulottunga I was associated with the Kalinga conquest, Kulottunga Cholapuram at Visakhapatnam and the title Sungam Tavirtta Chola.

s: Which Chola ruler took the title 'Madurai-konda'?
x: Parantaka I took the title Madurai-konda after capturing Madurai from the Pandyas.

s: Which Chola ruler took the title 'Pandita Chola'?
x: Rajendra I was called Pandita Chola as a patron of learning; he was also Gangaikonda Chola and Kadaram Kondan.

s: The title 'Yanai-mel-thunjina Devar' refers to the Chola king who:
o: Died on an elephant at Koppam
x: Rajadhiraja I was called Yanai-mel-thunjina Devar because he died on an elephant at Koppam.

s: Which Chola ruler bore the title Mummudi Chola, after which northern Sri Lanka was named 'Mummadichola Mandalam'?
x: Rajaraja I took the title Mummudi Chola; northern Sri Lanka was named Mummadichola Mandalam.

s: Rajendra I’s northern expedition of 1022 CE is particularly associated with which achievement?
o: Defeat of Vijayaditya VII at Kalidindi
Crossing the Ganga and defeating the Pala ruler Mahipala I
Conquest of Madurai and Sri Lanka
Defeat of the Rashtrakuta king Krishna III
x: In 1022 CE, Rajendra I led a northern campaign, crossed the Ganga and defeated the Pala ruler Mahipala I.

s: After his victory at Dharanikota over Vijayaditya VII and the Kalyani army, which Chola ruler burnt Kollipaka?
x: Rajadhiraja I won at Dharanikota and then burnt Kollipaka. Rajendra I's army won at Kalidindi, Virarajendra won at Kudalasangamam, and Kulottunga I later merged Vengi in 1075.

s: At the battle of Koppam in 1053 CE, which event occurred?
o: Virarajendra defeated Someshvara I and installed Vijayaditya VII.
Rajendra I defeated Vijayaditya VII at Kalidindi.
Rajadhiraja I killed Someshvara I and captured Kalyani.
Someshvara I killed Rajadhiraja I, while Rajendra II was crowned on the battlefield and claimed victory.
x: At Koppam, Someshvara I killed the Chola ruler Rajadhiraja I. Rajendra II was then crowned on the field and claimed victory.

s: Under which Chola ruler did the Cholas win the battle of Kudalasangamam?
x: Virarajendra won at Kudalasangamam; Krishna III's Rashtrakutas won Takkolam and Rajendra I's army won at Kalidindi.

s: What was the main cause of the Chola-Chalukya wars?
o: control of Vengi and the struggle for supremacy in the Deccan
competition over the port of Kolhapur alone
a religious conflict between Shaivism and Buddhism
a dispute over the succession to the Rashtrakuta throne alone
x: The wars arose mainly from succession disputes in Vengi, with each side backing a claimant, and from the wider struggle for supremacy in the Deccan.

s: Who defeated Parantaka I in the battle of Takkolam (949 CE)?
x: Takkolam was a Chola defeat: the Rashtrakuta Krishna III beat Parantaka I.

s:
Consider the following statements about Chola battles:
1. The Cholas won the battle of Takkolam.
2. Rajendra II was crowned on the battlefield of Koppam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Rajendra II was crowned at Koppam after Rajadhiraja I died; Takkolam (949) was won by the Rashtrakutas.

s: After the Chola victory at Kalidindi, who built three Shiva temples for the fallen Chola commanders?
x: Rajaraja Narendra built three Shiva temples for the Chola commanders who fell at Kalidindi.

s: Near which present-day town was the battle of Kalidindi fought?
x: Kalidindi, where Rajendra I's army defeated Vijayaditya VII and the Kalyani Chalukyas, is near Eluru.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Naval expedition against Kadaram and Srivijaya – c. 1035 CE
x: Thakkolam was fought in 949 CE. Brihadeeswara was completed in 1010 CE, the Kadaram–Srivijaya expedition sent in 1025 CE and Gangaikondacholapuram built around 1035 CE.

s: In May 2026, the Netherlands returned which Chola copper plates to India at The Hague?
x: On 16 May 2026 the Netherlands returned the Anaimangalam (Leiden) copper plates at The Hague. They were ordered by Rajaraja I, engraved under Rajendra I and extended by Kulottunga I.

s: In which city is the Grand Chola Museum, with a planned 125-ft statue of Rajaraja Chola, coming up?
x: In February 2026 the Grand Chola Museum at Thanjavur was announced with a planned 125-ft Rajaraja Chola statue on 52 acres.

s: Off which early Chola port-capital did Tamil Nadu begin the third phase of underwater exploration in September 2026?
x: On 8 September 2026 Tamil Nadu began the third phase of underwater exploration off Poompuhar, an early Chola capital.

s: In May 2026, which country returned the Leiden copper plates of the Cholas?
x: On 16 May 2026 the Netherlands returned the plates at The Hague, the first return of Chola copper plates.

s: Which of the following South Indian polities is described as highly centralised?
x: The Badami Chalukya polity is described as highly centralised, whereas Pallava, Chola and Rashtrakuta records show active local and village assemblies.

s: Who described the Chola system of elected assemblies, committees and lottery as an example of “grassroots democracy”?
x: Nilakanta Sastri regarded the Chola system as a remarkable example of grassroots democracy. Burton Stein is associated with the segmentary-state interpretation.

s: Which South Indian dynasty's sabha and ur assemblies formed the base on which the Cholas built their local self-government?
x: Sabha and ur assemblies already appear under the Pallavas; the Badami Chalukyas were highly centralised.

s: Which of the following South Indian dynasties is known for elected village assemblies and committees chosen by lottery?
x: The Cholas are known for village autonomy: elected assemblies, variyams (committees) and the kudavolai lottery.

s: Which historian described the Chola state as a 'segmentary state'?
x: Burton Stein called it a segmentary state where local autonomy stayed intact at the periphery; Nilakanta Sastri spoke of grassroots democracy.

s: How did Burton Stein describe the Chola state?
x: Burton Stein used the concept of a segmentary state, while K.A. Nilakanta Sastri presented a more centralised picture.

s: On which of the following were the extensive inscriptions that give a rich record of Chola history mainly engraved?
x: The Cholas engraved long inscriptions on temple walls, which give an unusually rich record of their history.

s: Under the Uttaramerur rules, how much land did a candidate for a Chola village committee have to own at least?
x: Qualifications included owning at least 1/4 veli of land, an own house, age 35-70 and Vedic knowledge; recent committee service was a disqualification.

s: The Uttaramerur inscriptions (919 and 921 CE) belong to which Chola ruler?
x: The two Uttaramerur inscriptions are of Parantaka I, dated 919 and 921 CE; Uttaramerur is in Kanchipuram district.

s: Which of the following was a qualification for membership of a Chola village committee?
x: Owning a residence was a qualification, whereas failure to submit accounts, committing sins and stealing property were disqualifications.

s: The Uttaramerur inscriptions are located in which district of Tamil Nadu?
x: Uttaramerur is in Kanchipuram district; its inscriptions are dated 919 and 921 CE under Parantaka I.

s: Under the Uttaramerur rules, what was the age limit for a candidate for a village committee?
x: The age qualification was 35 to 70 years, along with land, a house and Vedic learning.

s: For what are the Uttaramerur inscriptions of Parantaka I mainly known?
o: Rules for village assemblies and their committees
Rajendra I's naval expedition to Srivijaya
The grant of a village to the Chudamani Vihara
The destruction of the Chera navy at Kandalur Salai
x: The Uttaramerur inscriptions (919 and 921 CE) are the most detailed record of village administration, giving rules for the sabha and its variyams.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Uttaramerur inscriptions:
1. They are dated 919 and 921 CE.
2. They belong to the reign of Rajaraja I.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The two Uttaramerur inscriptions are dated 919 and 921 CE and belong to Parantaka I, not Rajaraja I.

s: Under the Uttaramerur rules, which of the following disqualified a person from a Chola village committee?
o: Being between 35 and 70 years of age
x: A person who had failed to submit accounts was barred; owning a house, Vedic learning and age 35–70 were qualifications.

s: In August 2025, the Prime Minister cited the 'ballot pot' of which place as proof of India's early democratic traditions?
x: PM Modi cited the kudavolai (ballot pot) of Uttaramerur in August 2025.

s: What did the term 'kudavolai' mean in Chola local administration?
o: A system of collecting land revenue
A lottery system using palm-leaf ballots placed in a pot
x: Kudavolai was the selection procedure in which names written on palm leaves were placed in a pot and drawn by lot.

s: What happened to a person who had served on a Chola village committee in the preceding three years?
o: Eligible only for a finance committee
x: Persons who had served on a committee during the previous three years were disqualified from selection.

s: Under the kudavolai system, the village was divided into how many wards (kudumbus)?
x: The village was split into 30 wards (kudumbus) for the lottery.

s: What was the term of members chosen by kudavolai for a Chola village committee?
x: Committee members served 360 days; those who had served in the past three years were barred.

s: Who drew the names from the pot in the kudavolai procedure?
x: A young boy or girl drew the palm-leaf names from the pot by lot.

s: Which of the following pairs of Chola terms is correctly matched?
x: Variyam meant committee; kudumbu was the ward, kudavolai the lottery and perumakkal the assembly members.

s: What was the name of the lottery system used to select members of the Chola village assembly?
x: The Cholas used the kudavolai lottery among qualified persons, whereas Panchayat members under the 73rd Amendment are directly elected.

s: In Chola village administration, who were the 'Variyapperumakkal'?
x: Variyapperumakkal were the elected members of the village committees (variyams).

s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents the areas covered by the committees recorded at Uttaramerur?
o: Foreign trade, naval warfare, diplomacy and coin minting
Royal succession, military conquest, espionage and taxation alone
Agricultural slavery, overseas colonisation, astronomy and medicine
x: The Uttaramerur record refers to committees dealing with irrigation, gardens, justice and finance.

s: Which of the following pairs of Chola village committees is correctly matched?
o: Pon variyam – Gold and financial matters
Samvatsara variyam – Tanks and distribution of water
x: Pon variyam dealt with gold and finance. Samvatsara variyam handled annual works, eri variyam tanks and water, and thotta variyam gardens.

s: What did the eri variyam of a Chola village look after?
x: The eri variyam managed tanks and the distribution of water to fields.

s: What did the pon variyam of a Chola village deal with?
x: Pon means gold: the pon variyam handled finance and checked currency.

s: What was the panchavara variyam in Chola villages?
x: The panchavara variyam was the standing (supervisory) committee; the samvatsara variyam was the annual committee.

s: Which variyam was the annual committee of a Chola village, also dealing with justice?
x: The samvatsara variyam was the annual committee for annual works and justice.

s: In the Chola period, whose assembly was the nattar?
o: merchants of the nadu's market town
Brahmin landholders of a single village
leading vellala landholders of the nadu
x: The nattar was the nadu assembly of leading vellala landholders, handling revenue and disputes above village level; the merchant body was the nagaram.

s: What was the nadu in Chola administration?
x: The ur was the village and the nadu a group of villages, whose assembly was the nattar.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Chola nattar:
1. It handled revenue collection and disputes above the village level.
2. It was a body created under the 73rd Amendment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The nattar handled revenue and disputes above village level; it was a Chola body, not a 73rd Amendment body.

s: In which villages was the 'ur' the general assembly of residents in Chola local administration?
x: Ur was the general assembly in ordinary non-brahmadeya, or vellanvagai, villages.

s: In Chola administration, whose assembly was the 'Nagaram'?
x: Nagaram was the body of merchant towns; Ur was the ordinary village assembly, Sabha the Brahmana village assembly, and Variyams were village committees.

s: In which villages did the Chola sabha (mahasabha) function?
x: The sabha met in brahmadeya (rent-free agrahara) villages and had Brahmans only; the ur was in non-brahmadeya villages.

s: Which temple did Rajaraja I direct the Cholamandalam sabhas to serve?
x: Rajaraja I directed the Cholamandalam sabhas to serve the Brihadeshvara temple.

s: In what form did Chola village assemblies collect royal dues?
x: Royal dues were collected in cash, kind or both; the assembly also owned village lands, raised loans, levied taxes and auctioned defaulters' land.

s: Which of the following was a power of Chola village assemblies?
o: Auctioning the land of tax defaulters
x: Assemblies levied taxes, raised loans and auctioned defaulters' land; they were absolute proprietors of village lands.

s:
Consider the following statements about Chola village assemblies:
1. They were the absolute proprietors of village lands.
2. They could raise loans.
3. They minted royal coins.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The assemblies owned village lands and could raise loans and levy taxes; minting coins was not their power.

s: Who among the following could take part in the Chola sabhas?
x: Sabha participation was tied to propertied, Vedic-learned Brahmins, so the system is criticised as elitist; it was not based on universal adult franchise.

s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correctly matched?
o: Nattar — direct universal adult franchise body under the 73rd Amendment
Burton Stein — segmentary state and local autonomy
Nilakanta Sastri — Chola local self-government as grassroots democracy
x: The nattar was a Chola nadu-level assembly of leading vellala landholders. It was not a body created under the 73rd Amendment and was not based on universal adult franchise.

s: Village mahajana assemblies, a weaker parallel to the Chola sabhas, are seen in the inscriptions of which Andhra dynasties?
x: Kakatiya and Velanati inscriptions show village mahajana assemblies.

s: Which of the following was a feature of Chola village assemblies, unlike the 73rd Amendment?
x: Chola assemblies had no women's quota, whereas Article 243D reserves at least one-third of seats for women.

s: Which Article of the Constitution recognises the Gram Sabha under the Panchayati Raj framework?
x: Article 243A deals with the Gram Sabha. Article 243C concerns the composition of Panchayats, Article 243D reservations, and Article 243E duration.

s: Under the 73rd Amendment, the intermediate tier of Panchayats may be omitted in a State whose population does not exceed:
x: The intermediate tier is optional in a State with a population not exceeding twenty lakh.

s: Which Article of the Constitution reserves not less than one-third of Panchayat seats for women?
x: Article 243D reserves one-third of Panchayat seats and chairperson posts for women, unlike the Chola village assemblies, which had no quota for women.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides a five-year term for Panchayats?
x: Article 243E gives Panchayats a five-year term and requires elections within six months of dissolution.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Kaikkolar referred to royal infantry regiments. Velaikkarar were loyal bodyguard troops, Kadagams were military cantonments, and Eri variyam was a tank committee.

s: Who were the Velaikkarar in the Chola military system?
o: Cavalry units recruited from Sri Lanka
Loyal bodyguard troops sworn to die with the king
Provincial governors appointed from among princes
x: The Velaikkarar were loyal bodyguard troops who were sworn to die with the king.

s: Which Chola ruler is credited with building the Chola navy?
x: Rajaraja I is credited with building the Chola navy. Rajendra I later expanded its operations significantly.

s: With which place is Kadaram, captured by Rajendra I's 1025 CE expedition against Srivijaya, identified?
x: Rajendra I's Srivijaya expedition took Kadaram (Kedah) in Malaya and parts of Sumatra.

s: What were the royal infantry regiments of the Chola army called?
x: Kaikkolar were the royal infantry regiments; Velaikkarar were bodyguards sworn to die with the king.

s: What were Chola military cantonments known as?
x: Kadagams were cantonments; ghatikas were colleges and kottams/valanadus administrative units.

s: The Chola navy made which water body a 'Chola Lake', in the words of K.A. Nilakanta Sastri?
x: Nilakanta Sastri said the Chola navy made the Bay of Bengal a 'Chola Lake'.

s: Where did Rajaraja I's navy destroy the Chera navy?
x: Rajaraja I, who built the Chola navy, destroyed the Chera navy at Trivandrum.

s: When was the successor (yuvaraja) generally named under the Cholas?
o: During the king's own lifetime, and made co-regent
By the nadu assembly in every case
x: Chola kings named the yuvaraja in their own lifetime and made him co-regent; Rajendra I became co-regent in 1012 and king in 1014.

s: What did Chola royal orders generally consist of?
o: A Sanskrit preamble followed by a Tamil operative part
Tamil genealogy followed by a Sanskrit grant
x: The royal orders had a Sanskrit preamble containing genealogy and conquests, followed by the Tamil operative portion.

s: Chola inscriptions praised the king as a warrior, a patron of the arts and the protector of what?
x: Chola kings were compared to gods, their images were installed beside deities, and inscriptions praised them as warriors, patrons of art and protectors of varnashrama dharma.

s: In which year did Rajendra I become co-regent?
x: Rajendra I was made co-regent in 1012 and became king in 1014.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Chola kingship?
o: The successor was named only after the king's death.
Images of kings and queens were placed beside deities.
Royal orders had a Sanskrit preamble and a Tamil operative part.
Rajaraja I was called Ulakalanda Perumal.
x: The Chola king named his successor in his own lifetime and made him co-regent; the other statements are correct.

s: Why was Rajaraja I given the title 'Ulakalanada Perumal'?
o: the king who abolished hereditary officials
the ruler who measured the earth, like Vishnu’s three strides
the conqueror of the entire island of Sri Lanka
the patron who built all the major Chola temples
x: Ulakalanada Perumal means one who measured the earth, an image associated with Vishnu’s three strides.

s: Which statement about Chola inscriptions is correct?
o: They were confined to military victories and contain no economic information.
They are mostly brief records written only in Sanskrit and unrelated to administration.
They were written primarily in Prakrit because Tamil was not used administratively.
They are among the most voluminous and detailed sources from South India, with Tamil as the language of administration.
x: Chola inscriptions are the most voluminous and detailed in South India, and Tamil was the language of administration.

s: With which of the following are the Tiruvalangadu copper plates mainly associated?
o: The genealogy and conquests of Rajendra I
The survey of land by Rajaraja I
The construction of the Grand Anicut by Karikala
The abolition of tolls by Kulottunga I
x: The Tiruvalangadu plates of Rajendra I provide Chola genealogy and accounts of conquests.

s: The Larger Leiden (Anaimangalam) plates record a grant to the Chulamanivarma-vihara built by the king of which kingdom?
x: The plates, ordered by Rajaraja I and engraved under Rajendra I, grant Anaimangalam village to the vihara built by the Srivijaya king Sri Mara Vijayotunga Varman; they use Sanskrit and Tamil.

s: The smaller Leiden plates associated with the Chudamani Vihara comprise:
o: 21 sheets and record the construction of the vihara by the Srivijaya king
21 sheets and record Rajaraja I’s original grant only
3 sheets and record Kulottunga I’s extension of the grant after an appeal by two Javanese envoys
3 sheets and record Rajendra I’s expedition to Kadaram
x: The smaller plates contain three sheets and record Kulottunga I’s extension of the grant after two Javanese envoys appealed to him.

s: To the reign of which Chola ruler do the Anbil plates, with a Sanskrit genealogy, belong?
x: The Anbil plates are of Sundara Chola; the Tiruvalangadu plates are of Rajendra I.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kadamai — Land revenue collected in kind
Vetti — Forced labour owed by villagers to the state
Irai — Compulsory feeding of state officials
x: Irai meant a tax or levy on land. The obligation to feed state officials was called Eccoru.

s: Which of the following pairs (Chola fiscal and labour terms) is correctly matched?
o: Kasu – rural tax collected in cash
x: Nettal denoted compulsory labour; Antarayam was a rural tax collected in cash, Eccoru the obligation to feed state officials and Kasu a gold coin.

s: What was the normal rate of Chola land revenue?
x: The normal Chola land revenue was one-sixth of the produce.

s: Which of the following terms collectively denoted forced labour service in Chola administration?
x: Vetti, Muttaiyal and Kudimai denoted forced labour service.

s: The Chola land tax of one-sixth of the produce was similar to the rate of which of the following?
x: The Chola rate of one-sixth matched the standard associated with the Pallavas and Kakatiyas. The Mughals and Sher Shah are associated with one-third, while the Gupta rate was about one-seventh.

s: Which Chola ruler is associated with the title ‘Sungam Tavirtta Chola’?
x: Kulottunga I was called Sungam Tavirtta Chola, meaning the Chola who abolished tolls.

s: What did 'Kadamai' denote in Chola revenue terms?
x: Kadamai was land revenue in kind; Antarayam was the rural tax in cash.

s: Which of the following pairs (Chola revenue terms) is correctly matched?
x: Ayam meant royal dues; Irai was the tax on land, Kasu the gold coin and Eccoru the duty to feed visiting officials.

s: With which Chola ruler is the land survey of the Chola empire associated?
x: The Chola land survey was carried out by Rajaraja I.

s: Through which body were tax remissions and exemptions granted under the Cholas?
x: Remissions were granted through the ur; ghatikas were colleges, kadagams cantonments and velaikkarar bodyguards.

s: What did 'Antarayam' denote in Chola revenue terms?
x: Antarayam was a rural tax paid in cash; kadamai was land revenue in kind.

s: What was 'Eccoru' in the Chola period?
x: Eccoru was the duty of villagers to feed visiting officials.

s: What did the term 'Devadana' mean in the Chola period?
o: Land used exclusively for tank repairs
x: Devadana lands were grants made to temples.

s: Which of the following pairs of Chola land terms is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Vellanvagai – land of non-Brahmin peasant proprietors
Salabhoga – land for maintaining a school
x: Pallichchandam was land donated to Jaina institutions; land gifted to temples was devadana.

s: In Chola land rights (kani), what did 'karanmai' mean?
x: Karanmai was the right to cultivate and mitachi the superior possessory right; ulukudi were tenants and kaniyudaiyar the land-owning farmers.

s: In the Chola period, for the maintenance of what was the revenue of 'eripatti' land set apart?
x: Eripatti revenue maintained the village tank; ghatikas were colleges attached to temples, and land gifted to temples was devadana.

s: To whom was 'Pallichchandam' land granted in the Chola period?
x: Pallichchandam was land given to Jaina institutions; Shalabhoga was land for a school.

s: For the maintenance of what was 'Shalabhoga' land meant in the Chola period?
x: Shalabhoga was land for a school; Eripatti maintained the village tank and Devadana went to temples.

s:
Consider the following statements about Chola land classification:
1. Brahmadeya was rent-free land granted to Brahmins.
2. Vellanvagai was the land of non-Brahmin peasants.
3. Taniyur was a village donated to a single Brahmin.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Brahmadeya and Vellanvagai are correctly described; Taniyur was a very large village run as one unit, not a single-Brahmin village.

s: What was a 'Taniyur' in the Chola kingdom?
o: A very large village administered as a single unit
A village donated to a single Brahmin
A group of villages forming a nadu
Land set apart for the maintenance of the village tank
x: Taniyur (or kottam) was a very large village run as one unit; calling it a village donated to a single Brahmin is wrong.

s: What were the colleges attached to temples in the Chola period called?
x: Ghatikas were colleges attached to temples; kadagams were cantonments and variyams were village committees.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Eripatti was land whose revenue was used to maintain the village tank.
2. Ghatikas were colleges attached to temples.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: eripatti revenue paid for the village tank, and ghatikas were temple colleges.

s: Who were the 'Ulukudi' in Chola land relations?
x: Kaniyudaiyar were land-owning farmers and Ulukudi were tenants.

s: In Chola land rights, what did 'Mitachi' mean?
x: Mitachi was the superior possessory right; karanmai was the right to cultivate.

s: The first phase of the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP) ran during:
x: The first phase ran from 2008 to 2016; 2016-26 was the second phase, which brought ULPIN (Bhu-Aadhaar).

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Adhikari — Royal officer supervising local bodies
Nattar — Members of the royal court of justice
x: An adhikari was a royal officer supervising local bodies. Perundaram were the highest officials, sirudaram were lower officials, and nattar were members of the nadu assembly.

s: Who wrote down the king’s oral orders on palm leaf in the Chola administration?
x: The tirumandira-olai was the royal secretary who recorded the king’s oral orders on palm leaf.

s: What was the main function of the olai-nayagam in Chola administration?
x: The olai-nayagam, or chief secretary, checked and countersigned royal orders before they were sent to officials.

s: What did the term 'Sirudaram' denote in Chola administration?
x: Sirudaram were the lower officials; Perundaram were the highest officials.

s: Who was the Chola royal officer who supervised local bodies?
x: The Adhikari was the royal officer supervising local bodies; Nattar were members of the nadu assembly.

s: Who were the 'Nattar' in Chola administration?
x: Nattar were the members of the nadu assembly; the highest officials were Perundaram.

s: Who was a 'Samanta' in the Chola political system?
o: A royal secretary who countersigned orders
A tank committee member elected by villagers
A temple servant given tax-free land
A defeated king restored after accepting overlordship, tribute and military obligations
x: A Samanta was a defeated king restored on condition that he accepted overlordship, paid tribute and provided military help.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Chola administrative units?
o: Nadu was a unit above the Ur.
Kottam or Valanadu was a unit below the Nadu.
x: The order from lowest to highest was Ur, Nadu, Kottam/Valanadu and Mandalam, so Kottam/Valanadu stood above the Nadu, not below it.

s: Which region was called Mummudicholamandalam?
x: Mummudicholamandalam denoted northern Sri Lanka and was so named by Rajaraja I.

s: How many Mandalams (provinces) did the Chola Empire have?
x: The Chola Empire had eight Mandalams, each under a viceroy or governor who could be a prince or noble.

s: In the Chola administrative hierarchy, of which unit was 'kurram' another name?
x: The order was Ur, Nadu (kurram), Kottam/Valanadu and Mandalam; kurram was the Nadu.

s: Which region was named Jayankondacholamandalam by the Cholas?
x: Jayankondacholamandalam was the former Pallava Tondaimandalam; Mummudicholamandalam was northern Sri Lanka.

s: What title did the sons of Kulottunga I who governed Vengi as viceroys bear?
x: Kulottunga I placed his sons in Vengi as viceroys called Rajapratinidhi.

s:
Consider the following statements about Chola provinces:
1. The empire had eight mandalams.
2. Each mandalam was under a viceroy, often a prince or noble.
3. Burton Stein described the Chola state as centralised.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: There were eight mandalams under viceroys, often princes; Burton Stein called the state segmentary, while Nilakanta Sastri called it centralised.

s: What were the Chola provincial territories that were not annexed but paid tribute known as?
x: Chola provincial territories included annexed principalities and samanta or vassal territories that paid tribute.

s: Which ruler is associated with the construction of Kallanai, also called the Grand Anicut?
x: Karikala Chola of the Sangam age built the Kallanai, or Grand Anicut, across the Kaveri for irrigation. Rajaraja I, Rajendra I and Kulottunga I were later imperial Cholas.

s: Besides being landholders, employers and lenders, Chola temples were venues for the meetings of which body?
x: Chola temples were major landholders, employers and lenders, and also provided venues for village assembly meetings.

s: From which land was the maintenance and repair of Chola village tanks financed?
x: Eripatti land was set aside to finance the maintenance and repair of village tanks.

s: Which committee was responsible for managing village tanks and distributing water to fields?
x: The eri variyam was the tank committee responsible for managing tanks and distributing water to fields.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Tank irrigation was a major feature of the Cholas' agricultural economy.
Kallanai was built by Karikala Chola.
Tank irrigation was unknown under the Vijayanagara rulers.
The Kakatiyas built large irrigation tanks.
x: Option C is incorrect: the Vijayanagara rulers built many tanks and reservoirs, such as the Porumamilla tank. Chola tank irrigation, Karikala's Kallanai and the large Kakatiya tanks are all correct.

s: Rajaraja I made the sabhas of Cholamandalam serve which temple?
x: Rajaraja I made the Cholamandalam sabhas serve the Brihadeeswara temple, showing the temple's role in administration.

s: Who built the Kallanai (Grand Anicut) on the Kaveri?
x: The Kallanai was built by Karikala; later Cholas kept up the delta channels.

s: Which merchant guild originated from Aihole and operated pan-regionally and overseas?
x: Ayyavole-500 originated from Aihole; Manigramam was a foreign-trade corporation, Ubhaya Nanadesi handled domestic and foreign trade, and Nagaram was a market-town assembly.

s: Who headed the Nakaras (merchant bodies) under the Eastern Chalukyas?
x: Nakaras headed by Shreshthis traded under the Eastern Chalukyas, and Ayyavole and Manigramam were active in Andhra, especially around Penugonda.

s: What were the Ayyavole 500 and Manigramam of the Chola age?
x: Ayyavole 500 and Manigramam were merchant guilds of the Chola age, part of a sea trade running from Sri Lanka through Malaya and Sumatra to Southeast Asia.

s: What happened to the independence of the merchant guilds as Chola power declined?
x: Merchant guilds, which had emblems and militias, acted as bankers and donated to temples, became more independent as the Cholas declined.

s: Which merchant body of the Chola age handled both domestic and foreign trade?
x: Ubhaya Nanadesi engaged in both domestic and foreign trade; Nagaram was local and Nanadesi foreign.

s: What was 'Nagaram' (Nakaram) in the Chola age?
o: Local merchant assembly of a market town
x: Nagaram was the local merchant assembly of a market town; Manigramam and Nanadesi were foreign-trade bodies.

s: Whose guild was the Anjuvannam?
x: Anjuvannam was the guild of West Asian foreign merchants.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Chola merchant guilds?
o: They had their own symbols and militias.
They were confined to local trade alone.
x: Guilds such as Ayyavole-500 and Manigramam carried inter-regional and overseas trade; the other features are correct.

s: How many branches did the merchant guilds of Penugonda have across Vengi?
x: Penugonda was the main trade centre of medieval Andhra, where Ayyavole and Manigramam had 18 branches across Vengi.

s: Which place was a trade centre between Kalyan and Vengi?
x: Tagara was the trade centre on the route between Kalyan and Vengi; the others were ports.

s: Which merchant guilds were active at Penugonda, the main trade centre of medieval Andhra?
x: Ayyavole and Manigramam were active in Andhra, especially at Penugonda, with 18 branches across Vengi.

s: Which merchant guild's name meant 'of many countries' and dealt in foreign trade?
x: Nanadesi (also called Pekkundru) means 'of many countries' and was a foreign-trade guild.

s: The king of which kingdom built the Chudamani Vihara at Nagapattinam?
x: The Buddhist Chudamani Vihara was built by the Srivijaya king Sri Mara Vijayottunga Varman.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Chola temple economy:
1. Temple income came from guild donations and royal grants of land and paddy.
2. Rajaraja I granted the village of Anaimangalam to the Chudamani Vihara.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: temples drew on guild donations and royal grants, and the Larger Leiden plates record Rajaraja I's grant of Anaimangalam.

s: Which Srivijaya king built the Chudamani Vihara at Nagapattinam in 1006?
x: Sri Mara Vijayottunga Varman built the Chudamani Vihara in 1006; Rajaraja I granted it Anaimangalam.

s: Where was the vihara linked with the early friendly relations between the Cholas and Srivijaya?
x: Chola-Srivijaya relations began amicably, as seen in the Nagapattinam vihara, until obstruction of Indian traders led to Rajendra I's 1025 expedition to Kadaram.

s: The wider historical significance of the Chola merchant-guild networks was that they:
o: replaced all temple institutions with royal agencies
confined trade to inland Tamil markets
ended commercial contacts with China and Southeast Asia
carried Chola trade and Dravidian culture across the Bay of Bengal
x: The guild networks extended Chola commerce and Dravidian cultural influence across the Bay of Bengal.

s: In which year did Kulottunga I send 72 merchants to China?
x: Kulottunga I sent 72 merchants to China in 1077; Chola embassies had reached the Song court in 1015 and 1033.

s: Under which Chola ruler did relations with Srivijaya turn hostile over the China route?
x: Relations were friendly under Rajaraja I but turned hostile under Rajendra I, who sent the 1025 expedition.

s: Chola embassies of 1015 and 1033 reached the court of which Chinese dynasty?
x: Chola embassies reached the Song court in 1015 and 1033.

s: Where was the 1088 Tamil inscription of the Ayyavole-500 merchant guild found?
x: Barus (Lobu Tua) has the 1088 Ayyavole-500 inscription; Takua Pa names Manigramam and Pagan has a Nanadesi Vishnu temple inscription.

s: The Tamil inscription at Takua Pa in Thailand names which guild?
x: The Takua Pa inscription names Manigramam; Pagan in Myanmar has a Nanadesi Vishnu temple.

s: Which of the following pairs (guild record abroad – place) is correctly matched?
x: The Nanadesi Vishnu temple is at Pagan (Myanmar); the 1088 Ayyavole-500 inscription is at Barus and Takua Pa names Manigramam.

s: Which was the main port of the Cholas, where the Chudamani Vihara stood?
x: Nagapattinam was the main Chola port and site of the Chudamani Vihara.

s: In which of the following is Quilon (Kollam), a centre of Arab and Chinese trade, located?
x: Quilon is a Kerala port where Arab and Chinese traders came.

s: At the mouth of which river did Kaveripattinam (Puhar), the port of the Sangam Cholas, lie?
x: Kaveripattinam was the Sangam Chola port at the mouth of the Kaveri.

s: Which one of the following represents the correct classification of major exports and imports in Chola overseas trade?
o: Exports: horses and porcelain; Imports: textiles and pepper
Exports: textiles, pepper and precious stones; Imports: horses, Chinese silk, porcelain, camphor and aromatics
Exports: Chinese silk and horses; Imports: paddy and land grants
Exports: camphor and aromatics; Imports: spices and precious stones only
x: The principal exports included textiles, pepper and precious stones. Imports included horses, Chinese silk and porcelain, camphor and aromatics.

s: Which of the following was an import, not an export, in Chola overseas trade?
x: Horses were imported; textiles, pepper and precious stones were exported.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched in Chola overseas trade?
x: Pepper was an export; the other pairs are correct.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the principal west-coast trade associated with Arab merchants and the foreign-merchant body Anjuvannam?
o: Trade in silk and porcelain; Anjuvannam represented local market assemblies
Trade in paddy and land; Anjuvannam represented craft guilds
Trade in precious stones and textiles; Anjuvannam represented royal officers
Trade in horses and spices; Anjuvannam represented foreign merchants
x: Arab trade on the west coast prominently involved horses and spices, while Anjuvannam was associated with foreign merchants.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
x: Kasu was a gold coin. Nagarams were market centres, Erivirappattanas were protected mercantile towns, and Kaveripattinam was a port and early Chola capital.

s: Which was the early port-capital of the Cholas?
x: Kaveripattinam was the early port-capital; Nagapattinam was the later chief port.

s: What were 'Erivirappattanas' in the Chola age?
x: Erivirappattanas were protected towns; Nagarams were market centres and Kasu a gold coin.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Chola foreign trade?
o: Chola embassies reached China in 1015 and 1033.
Kaveripattinam was the chief port of the later Cholas.
Conflict with Srivijaya arose over the China route.
Arabs on the west coast traded in horses and spices.
x: Nagapattinam was the chief port; Kaveripattinam was the early port-capital.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kaveripattinam — Port at the mouth of the Kaveri
x: Kaveripattinam, not Nagapattinam, was the early Chola capital and a port at the mouth of the Kaveri.

s: What does the lower right hand in abhaya mudra signify in the Chola Nataraja bronze?
x: Abhaya mudra means 'fear not', i.e. protection; the standard Nataraja is four-armed and the lower left hand points to the raised left foot.

s: What do the man's earring in the right ear and the woman's earring in the left ear of the Chola Nataraja symbolise?
o: the fusion of male and female principles
x: The different earrings of the Nataraja image represent the fusion of male and female principles.

s: What does the damaru held in the upper right hand of the Nataraja image symbolise?
x: The damaru symbolises creation, the agni in the upper left hand destruction, and the prabhamandala the cosmic cycle; Apasmara represents ignorance.

s: What is the lost-wax technique, perfected by the Cholas for making bronze icons, known as?
x: The Cholas perfected the cire perdue, or lost-wax, casting technique for bronze icons.

s: What does the dwarf Apasmara under the right foot of the Chola Nataraja symbolise?
x: Apasmara stands for ignorance; the damaru is creation, agni destruction and abhaya protection.

s: What does the agni (fire) in the upper left hand of the Nataraja image symbolise?
x: Agni in the upper left hand stands for destruction; the damaru in the upper right stands for creation.

s: Why are Rajaraja I's inscriptions at the Thanjavur temple significant?
o: The election of village assemblies through the Kudavolai system
Only the names of foreign merchants visiting the Chola ports
About 400 temple dancing women, musicians and temple staff supported by grants
The complete list of Nayanar hymns in the Tirumurai
x: The inscriptions mention about 400 temple dancing women and also refer to musicians and other staff who were paid through grants. The Kudavolai election system is recorded in Uttiramerur inscriptions.

s: For their reference to what are the Uttiramerur inscriptions of the time of Parantaka I especially important?
o: Kudavolai system of village assembly elections
x: The Uttiramerur inscriptions, associated with Parantaka I, record the Kudavolai or pot-ballot system used in village assembly elections.

s: At which places do Chola inscriptions record temple Vedic colleges?
x: Chola inscriptions record Vedic colleges at Ennayiram and Tribhuvani (near Pondicherry).

s: The Nagara style of temple architecture emerged prominently in which region and period?
o: The Deccan from about the 8th century CE
North India from about the 5th century CE
South India from about the 3rd century CE
Eastern India from about the 10th century CE
x: The Nagara style is associated with North India and is identified from about the 5th century CE.

s: Which dynasty started the Vesara style of temple architecture?
x: Vesara, blending Dravida vimana tiers with the Nagara curvilinear profile, was pioneered by the Badami Chalukyas; the Hoysalas came later.

s: With which of the following is the Nagara style of temple architecture associated?
x: The Nagara temple has a curvilinear shikhara, while the Dravida temple has a pyramidal vimana and elaborate prakara walls and gateways.

s: What is the topmost, dome-like crowning part of the vimana called?
x: Shikhara denotes the topmost, dome-like crowning portion of the vimana; the monolithic shikhara of the Thanjavur temple is especially noted.

s: Which one of the following correctly explains the term ‘Garbhagriha’ in Dravida temple architecture?
o: The womb-house containing the principal icon
The pillared hall used for gatherings
The raised platform of the temple
x: Garbhagriha literally denotes the womb-house and houses the principal deity or icon of the temple.

s: What is the 'antarala' in temple architecture?
o: vestibule between the sanctum and the mandapa
x: The antarala is the vestibule between sanctum and mandapa; the mandapa is a pillared hall, the jagati a raised platform and the gopuram the entrance gateway.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Virupaksha is at Hampi. Lingaraj is in Bhubaneswar, Jagannath in Puri and Dilwara at Mount Abu.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Khajuraho temples are in the Nagara style. Kailasanathar is Rajasimha style, the Mahabalipuram Rathas are Mamalla style and Chausath Yogini is circular.

s: The Draksharama Bhimeswara temple in Andhra Pradesh is built in which style?
x: Draksharama Bhimeswara is in the Chalukya-Chola style; Padmakshi at Hanamkonda is Kakatiya.

s: What is the pillared hall of a Dravida temple called?
x: The mandapa is the pillared hall; antarala is the vestibule, jagati the platform and prakara the enclosure walls.

s: What does 'prakara' refer to in temple architecture?
x: Prakara means the enclosure walls; the raised platform is the jagati.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
x: Option C is incorrect: the Dilwara Jain temples are at Mount Abu in Rajasthan, while Morena is known for the circular Chausath Yogini temple. Jagannath–Puri, Virupaksha–Hampi and Konark–Odisha are right.

s: What is the pyramidal tower over the garbhagriha of a Dravida temple called?
x: In the Dravida style the vimana is the pyramidal tower over the garbhagriha (sanctum).

s: Which of the following temples has a Dravida-style pinnacle with Nagara-style ornament?
x: The Teli temple at Gwalior has a Dravida pinnacle with Nagara ornament; the other three are Nagara temples.

s: Who founded the Jagannath temple at Puri?
x: The Jagannath temple at Puri was founded by Anantavarman Chodaganga of the Eastern Gangas.

s: In which style is the Kailasanathar temple at Kanchi built?
x: The Kailasanathar temple at Kanchi is in the Rajasimha style of Narasimhavarman II; the Mahabalipuram Rathas are Mamalla style.

s: The Kapoteswara temple, first Buddhist and later Shaiva, is located at which place in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Kapoteswara temple at Chejarla was a Buddhist shrine later turned Shaiva.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Padmakshi temple at Hanamkonda is a Kakatiya temple, not Pallava.

s: The Dashavatara temple at Devgarh belongs to which period?
x: The Dashavatara temple at Devgarh is a Gupta temple, not a Chandela temple of Khajuraho.

s: Chola temples represent the zenith of which temple style?
x: Chola free-standing structural temples are the zenith of the Dravida style, not Nagara; the style continued under the Kalyani Chalukyas and Hoysalas.

s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the comparative development of Dravidian art?
o: The Pallavas laid its foundation and the Cholas developed it on a monumental scale.
The Cholas laid its foundation and the Pallavas built its monumental culmination.
The Rashtrakutas alone created the Dravidian tradition.
The Hoysalas laid its foundation and the Kakatiyas completed it.
x: The comparison states that the Pallavas laid the foundation of Dravidian art, while the Cholas built its monumental culmination.

s: What is the name of the many-storeyed entrance gateway of a Dravida temple?
x: The gopuram is the many-storeyed entrance gateway; the vimana is the tower over the sanctum.

s: The Brihadeeswara Temple is also known by which of the following names?
x: Brihadeeswara Temple is also called Dakshina Meru.

s: The granite vimana of the Brihadeeswara temple at Thanjavur is about how high?
x: The vimana is about 216 feet high with a monolithic capstone of about 80 tonnes, and is built of granite, not brick.

s: The 'Musical Steps' and the horse-drawn stone chariot are features of which Chola temple?
x: The Musical Steps and stone chariot belong to the Airavatesvara temple at Darasuram, built by Rajaraja II; Kulottunga III built the Kampaharesvara at Tribhuvanam.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the vimana of the Gangaikondacholapuram Temple?
o: It is 216 feet high and has a straight, rigid profile.
It is 216 feet high and has a circular plan.
It is 180 feet high and is entirely made of brick and mortar.
It is 180 feet high and has a concave curvilinear profile.
x: The vimana of Gangaikondacholapuram is about 180 feet high and has a curvilinear concave profile.

s: With which temple is the Chit Sabha, with carvings of 108 classical dance poses, associated?
x: The Chit Sabha of the Thillai Nataraja Temple at Chidambaram contains carvings of 108 classical dance poses.

s: Who built the Airavatesvara temple at Darasuram?
x: Rajaraja II built the Airavatesvara temple; Rajaraja I built Brihadeeswara, Rajendra I built Gangaikondacholapuram and Kulottunga I abolished tolls.

s: Which of the following temple sites is part of the UNESCO group 'Great Living Chola Temples'?
x: The group comprises the temples at Thanjavur, Gangaikondacholapuram and Darasuram; Chidambaram is not included.

s: Among the following, which is the latest in chronological order?
x: The order is Seven Pagodas, Shore Temple, Brihadeeswara and then Gangaikondacholapuram, which came last.

s: Who built the Kampaharesvara temple at Tribhuvanam?
x: Kampaharesvara, Tribhuvanam is a late Chola temple of Kulottunga III; Darasuram was built by Rajaraja II.

s: Who built the Gangaikondacholapuram temple?
x: Rajendra I built Gangaikondacholapuram; Rajaraja I built the Brihadeeswara at Thanjavur.

s: In which year was the Brihadeeswara Temple, Thanjavur, first inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
x: Thanjavur was listed in 1987; in 2004 the listing was extended as the Great Living Chola Temples.

s: What is the approximate weight of the capstone of the Brihadeeswara vimana?
x: The granite vimana, about 216 ft high, carries a capstone of about 80 tonnes.

s: Where is the early Chola Koranganatha temple located?
x: The Koranganatha temple at Srinivasanallur is an early Chola structural temple.

s: What do the paintings in the dark ambulatory passage of the Brihadeeswara temple depict?
o: The Alvars composing the Divya Prabandham
Shiva as Tripurantaka and portraits of Rajaraja I with Karuvur Thevar
Only scenes from the Kalinga war
The coronation of Kulottunga II by Ottakuthar
x: The Brihadeeswara frescoes show Shiva as Tripurantaka and royal portraits of Rajaraja I together with his guru Karuvur Thevar.

s: What do the Chola-period cave paintings at Narthamalai depict?
x: The Chola-period paintings at Narthamalai show Shiva and Parvati. Chola murals are also found at Gangaikondacholapuram.

s: Who is the guru shown with Rajaraja I in the Brihadeeswara frescoes?
x: The frescoes of the dark ambulatory show Rajaraja I with his guru Karuvur Thevar.

s: Who compiled the Saiva canon Tirumurai in the time of Rajaraja I?
x: Nambi Andar Nambi compiled the Tirumurai, the 12-book Saiva canon of Nayanar hymns (Periya Puranam the 12th); it does not include the Vaishnava Alvar hymns.

s: Who is the author of the Periyapuranam, which describes the lives of the 63 Nayanars?
x: Sekkilar authored Periyapuranam, also called Tiruttondarpuranam, dealing with the lives of the 63 Nayanars.

s: Who is the author of the Tamil grammar Nannul?
x: Nannul is by Pavanandhi; Kalingattupparani is by Jayamkondar, Moovar Ula by Ottakuthar and Nalavenba by Pugalendi.

s: Who is the author of the Kalingattupparani, on Kulottunga I's Kalinga war?
x: Jayamkondar wrote Kalingattupparani; Ottakuthar wrote Moovar Ula.

s: Who compiled the Nalayira Divya Prabandham?
x: Nathamuni compiled the 4,000 verses of the 12 Alvars; Nambi Andar Nambi compiled the Saiva Tirumurai.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Tirumurai:
1. It was compiled by Nambi Andar Nambi in the time of Rajaraja I.
2. With the Periya Puranam it makes up 12 books.
3. It includes the hymns of the Alvars.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; the Tirumurai is a Saiva canon and has no Alvar hymns, which are in the Divya Prabandham.

s: Which of the following pairs (work – author) is correctly matched?
x: Moovar Ula is by Ottakuthar; Nalavenba is by Pugalendi, Nannul by Pavanandhi and Periya Puranam by Sekkilar.

s: Who is the author of the Kamba Ramayanam (Ramavataram)?
x: Kamban wrote the Kamba Ramayanam, a Tamil retelling of the Ramayana, not a mere translation.

s: Who is the author of the Nalavenba?
x: Nalavenba was written by Pugalendi; Jayamkondar wrote Kalingattupparani and Pavanandhi wrote Nannul.

s: The Nalayira Divya Prabandham compiled by Nathamuni contains 4,000 verses of how many Alvars?
x: The Nalayira Divya Prabandham has 4,000 verses of the 12 Alvars; 63 is the number of Nayanars.

s: Who built the Hoysaleswara (Shiva) temple at Halebid?
x: Ketamalla, an officer of Vishnuvardhana, built the Hoysaleswara temple (c. 1121); Vishnuvardhana himself built the Chennakeshava at Belur (1117).

s: The Keshava temple at Somanathapura (1268) was built by Somanatha, the general of which Hoysala ruler?
x: The Vishnu (Keshava) temple at Somanathapura was built in 1268 by Somanatha, general of Narasimha III.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Hoysalas?
o: Belur was the earlier Hoysala capital.
Dwarasamudra (Halebidu) was the later Hoysala capital.
The Hoysaleshwara temple at Halebidu is dedicated to Vishnu.
The Chennakeshava temple was built by Vishnuvardhana.
x: The Hoysaleshwara at Halebidu is a Shiva temple, so that statement is false; the other three are correct.

s: The Madanika (Salabhanjika) bracket figures are especially associated with which Hoysala temple site?
x: The Madanika bracket figures are associated with Belur, not Somanathapura.

s: Which one of the following temples is noted for having the best-preserved star-shaped plan?
x: The Keshava Temple at Somanathapura is regarded as having the best-preserved star-shaped plan.

s: To which deity is the Hoysaleswara temple at Halebid dedicated?
x: Hoysaleswara at Halebid is a Shiva temple; the Chennakeshava (Belur) and Keshava (Somanathapura) temples are Vishnu temples.

s: In which year did Vishnuvardhana build the Chennakeshava temple at Belur?
x: Vishnuvardhana built the Chennakeshava temple at Belur in 1117; Hoysaleswara dates to c. 1121 and Somanathapura to 1268.

s: What does the name 'Hoysaleswara' of the Halebid temple mean?
x: Hoysaleswara means 'Lord of the Hoysalas'; the temple was built in dark schist.

s: Of which soft stone were the Hoysala temples with lathe-turned pillars and star-shaped plans built?
x: Hoysala temples used soft chlorite schist (soapstone), had stellate plans and lathe-turned pillars, and were richly carved.

s: Hoysala temple architecture is generally classified under which style?
x: Hoysala architecture is generally classified as Vesara in examination keys, although it is also described as an evolution of the Dravida style.

s: What was the raised platform of about one metre, on which Hoysala temples with stellate plans were built, called?
x: Hoysala temples stand on a raised jagati platform of about one metre, and their stellate plan peaked in the twelfth century.

s: Which statement about Hoysala pillars is NOT correct?
o: They could include leaping lion or horse heads.
They could be carved into three or four sections on a single base.
They were generally left unpolished to preserve the rough texture of soapstone.
x: Hoysala pillars were finely polished, not generally left rough. They could have three or four sections on one base, leaping animal heads, and influenced Vijayanagara architecture.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Jakanachari is linked with Belur; Mallitamma with Somanathapura, Madanikas with Belur, and Ketamalla built the Hoysaleswara at Halebid.

s: Which sculptor is associated with the Keshava temple at Somanathapura?
x: Mallitamma is the sculptor linked with Somanathapura; Ketamalla and Somanatha were builders, and Jakanachari is linked with Belur.

s: Under which dynasty did the star-shaped (stellate) temple plan, which peaked under the Hoysalas, first begin?
x: The star plan began under the Chalukyas (6th c.) and peaked under the Hoysalas (12th c.); the Kalyani Chalukyas passed on soapstone and star plans.

s: In which year were the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List?
x: The Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage property in 2023.

s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the UNESCO 'Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas'?
x: The three components are Chennakeshava (Belur), Hoysaleswara (Halebid) and Keshava (Somanathapura).

s: Which is the only Shiva temple among the three Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas?
x: Hoysaleswara at Halebid is the only Shiva temple of the three; Belur and Somanathapura are Vishnu temples.

s: Which one of the following was the earlier capital of the Hoysalas?
x: Belur was the earlier capital of the Hoysalas, before Dwarasamudra became their capital.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Kanchi was the Pallava capital. Warangal was Kakatiya, Dwarasamudra Hoysala and Madurai Pandya.

s: What does the name Halebidu, taken after Dwarasamudra was sacked by the Delhi armies, mean?
x: Halebidu means 'old city'; the name came after the Delhi armies sacked Dwarasamudra.

s: Halebid, the modern name of the Hoysala capital Dwarasamudra, lies in which district of Karnataka?
x: Halebid (Halebidu), the old Dwarasamudra, is in Hassan district, Karnataka; Belur is also in Hassan.

s: The Hoysala Dynasty was associated primarily with which region?
x: The Hoysalas ruled from the Karnataka region, with capitals at Belur and later Dwarasamudra (Halebidu).

s: After his victory over whom did Vishnuvardhana assume the title 'Talakadugonda'?
x: Vishnuvardhana defeated the Cholas at Talakad and assumed the title Talakadugonda.

s: Which Hoysala ruler made the Hoysalas independent after defeating Yadava Bhillama?
x: Veera Ballala II defeated Yadava Bhillama and made the Hoysalas independent; his reign is given as 1170–1220.

s: Which event is associated with Narasimha III?
o: Victory over the Cholas at Talakad
Defeat of Yadava Ramachandra’s forces in 1305
x: Narasimha III was defeated by the Pandya ruler Maravarman Kulasekhara. The Keshava Temple at Somanathapura was also built during his reign.

s: Which Hoysala figure was an early chief under the Western Chalukyas?
x: Nripa Kama II was an early Hoysala chief under the Western Chalukyas; Veera Ballala II later made the Hoysalas independent.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Hoysalas:
1. They became independent by the close of the 12th century.
2. Their rule ended at the beginning of the 14th century.
3. They set up their kingdom in the early 8th century AD.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Hoysalas were independent by the close of the 12th century and ended at the beginning of the 14th; they did not set up their kingdom in the early 8th century.

s: Which Hoysala king was defeated by the Kakatiya commander Pedarudru after 1316?
x: Ballala III (1295–1342) beat Yadava Ramachandra's forces in 1305 but was defeated by Kakatiya commander Pedarudru after 1316.

s: Which Hoysala king defeated the forces of Yadava Ramachandra in 1305?
x: Ballala III (1295–1342) beat Yadava Ramachandra's forces in 1305; he was the last great Hoysala king.

s: What was the original name of Vishnuvardhana?
x: Vishnuvardhana was originally known as Bittideva, also called Bittiga.

s: Under whose influence did the Hoysala king Vishnuvardhana (Bittideva) convert from Jainism to Vaishnavism?
x: Bittideva became a Vaishnava under Ramanuja, who had taken refuge from Chola persecution; his queen Shantala Devi remained a Jain.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Veeragallu (hero stone) found at Neeragunda?
o: It may settle the date of Malik Kafur's death
It was found in Arsikere taluk
It may settle the date of Vishnuvardhana's death
x: The hero stone, unearthed on 28 June 2026 at Neeragunda (Arsikere taluk), may help settle the disputed date of Vishnuvardhana's death, not Malik Kafur's.

s: Which queen of Vishnuvardhana remained a Jain even after his conversion to Vaishnavism?
x: Vishnuvardhana's queen Shantala Devi remained a Jain though the king turned Vaishnava under Ramanuja.

s: Ramanuja came into the Hoysala kingdom while fleeing the persecution of which dynasty?
x: Ramanuja had fled Chola persecution into Hoysala land, where he converted Vishnuvardhana to Vaishnavism.

s: In which year did Ballala III die, after which the Hoysala territory passed to Vijayanagara?
x: Ballala III died in 1342, and the political space of the Hoysala kingdom then passed to Vijayanagara.

s: In the constant Hoysala–Yadava wars, which Yadava ruler of Devagiri defeated the Hoysalas?
x: Singhana defeated the Hoysalas; Mahadeva Yadava, by contrast, was defeated by them, and Bhillama was beaten by Veera Ballala II.

s: In which year did Malik Kafur take the Hoysala capital Dwarasamudra?
x: Malik Kafur took Dwarasamudra in 1311 in a campaign affecting the Yadavas, Kakatiyas, Hoysalas and Pandyas.

s: Who killed the Hoysala king Ballala III at Kannanur in 1342?
x: Ballala III was killed in 1342 by Ghiyas-ud-din, Sultan of Madurai, at Kannanur; Hoysala land then passed to Vijayanagara.

s: Which Yadava ruler threw off Kalyani Chalukya overlordship and founded Devagiri as the capital?
x: Bhillama V founded Devagiri (c. 1187) after throwing off Kalyani Chalukya overlordship; the Seuna Yadavas' mother tongue was Marathi.

s: Who renamed Devagiri, the Yadava capital, as Daulatabad?
x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq renamed Devagiri Daulatabad in 1327 when he shifted his capital there.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Yadavas of Devagiri:
1. They were also called the Seuna Yadavas.
2. They were first feudatories of the Western (Kalyani) Chalukyas.
3. Their capital Devagiri was founded by Shankaradeva.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Seuna Yadavas began as feudatories of the Kalyani Chalukyas; Devagiri was founded by Bhillama V (c. 1187), not Shankaradeva.

s: Which language did the Yadavas of Devagiri use as the language of scholarship?
x: The Yadavas spoke Marathi, but Sanskrit was their language of scholarship.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Yadavas of Devagiri:
1. Their mother tongue was Marathi.
2. They made Telugu their court language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Yadavas' mother tongue was Marathi and they encouraged it; Telugu was not their court language.

s: Which Yadava ruler was known as the greatest of the Yadava rulers and assumed the title ‘Teluguraya Sthapanacharya’?
x: Singhana II (c. 1210–1246) was the greatest Yadava ruler. He bore the title Teluguraya Sthapanacharya, 'installer of the Telugu king'.

s: Which Yadava ruler’s attack on the Kakatiyas was repulsed by Rudramadevi?
x: Rudramadevi repulsed the attack launched by Yadava ruler Mahadeva against the Kakatiyas.

s: During whose invasion was the last Yadava ruler Harapaladeva killed?
x: Harapaladeva was killed in Mubarak Khalji's invasion of 1317-18; Shankaradeva died during Malik Kafur's invasion in 1313.

s: Who was the last ruler of the Yadavas of Devagiri?
x: Harapaladeva (1313–1317) was the last Yadava ruler; he was killed in Mubarak Khalji's invasion.

s: Which daughter of Ganapatideva did the Yadava ruler Jaitugi marry to him after releasing him?
x: Jaitugi released Ganapatideva in 1199 and married his daughter Somaladevi to him.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ramachandra — Defeated by Alauddin Khalji's raid of 1296
Shankaradeva — Founded Devagiri as the Yadava capital
x: Devagiri was founded as the Yadava capital by Bhillama V, not Shankaradeva. The other three pairs are correctly matched.

s: Sarangapanideva, who later served at Rudramadevi's court, was the son of which Yadava ruler?
x: Singhana II's son Sarangapanideva served at Rudramadevi's court.

s: Singhana II released Ganapatideva as a counterweight to Hoysala Veera Ballala II's push into which region?
x: Ganapatideva was released to check Veera Ballala II's advance into the Krishna–Tungabhadra region.

s: Which record of Ramachandra confirms that Jaitugi killed Rudradeva and held Ganapatideva captive?
x: The Paithan copper plate of Ramachandra confirms Jaitugi's killing of Rudradeva and capture of Ganapatideva; the Bidar fort inscription records Rudramadevi's victory.

s: Hemadri served as Shrikaranadhipa under which Yadava rulers?
x: Hemadri served Mahadeva and Ramachandra as Shrikaranadhipa, the head of the secretariat or records.

s: Sarngadeva, author of the Sangita Ratnakara, was the court musician of which Yadava ruler?
x: Sarngadeva was court musician of Singhana II, at whose court the astronomer Changadeva also served.

s: Which astronomer was a court scholar of the Yadava ruler Singhana II?
x: Singhana II's court had the musician Sarngadeva and the astronomer Changadeva, grandson of Bhaskaracharya.

s: The Dnyaneshwari, written in 1290 at Nevasa, is a Marathi commentary on which text?
x: The Dnyaneshwari is a Marathi commentary on the Gita, written in 1290 at Nevasa in the reign of Ramachandra.

s: Who established the school at Patan for teaching Bhaskaracharya's works?
x: Changadeva, an astronomer and grandson of Bhaskaracharya, established the school at Patan; Sarngadeva was associated with music.

s: Who wrote the Sangita Ratnakara, a basic text of both Hindustani and Carnatic music?
x: Sarngadeva, the court musician of Singhana II, wrote the Sangita Ratnakara.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Chakradhar Swami — Founder of the Mahanubhava sect
Dnyaneshwar — Founder of the Mahanubhava sect
x: The Mahanubhava sect was founded by Chakradhar Swami. Dnyaneshwar composed the Dnyaneshwari; he did not found the Mahanubhava sect.

s: Which of the following pairs (work – author) is correctly matched?
x: Lilacharitra, the first Marathi prose, is by Mhaimbhat; Sangita Ratnakara is Sarngadeva's, Dnyaneshwari Dnyaneshwar's and Chaturvarga Chintamani Hemadri's.

s: Changadeva, who set up a school at Patan, was the grandson of whom?
x: Changadeva, astronomer at Singhana II's court, was the grandson of Bhaskaracharya and taught his works at Patan.

s: In whose reign was the Dnyaneshwari written at Nevasa in 1290?
x: Dnyaneshwar wrote the Dnyaneshwari, a Marathi commentary on the Gita, at Nevasa in 1290, in Ramachandra's reign.

s: What does Hemadri's Sanskrit work Chaturvarga Chintamani deal with?
o: dharma, rituals, charity, pilgrimage and vratas
x: Chaturvarga Chintamani is a Sanskrit encyclopaedia dealing with dharma, rituals, charity, pilgrimage and vratas.

s: Which architectural style is traditionally credited to Hemadri?
x: Hemadri is credited with the Hemadpanti style of temple architecture.

s: What type of masonry is Hemadpanti architecture, which used local black basalt with dressed stones interlocked without mortar?
x: Hemadpanti buildings interlocked dressed black basalt stones without mortar, a technique known as dry masonry.

s: Which statement about Hemadri’s account of Kakatiya Rudra is correct?
o: He claimed that Jaitugi captured and sacrificed Rudra.
He stated that Rudra founded the Hemadpanti style.
He recorded that Rudra served as Shrikaranadhipa.
He claimed that Rudra captured and sacrificed Jaitugi.
x: Hemadri, the Yadava minister and scholar, claimed that Jaitugi captured and sacrificed the Kakatiya Rudra.

s:
Consider the following statements about Hemadri:
1. He was Shrikaranadhipa, head of the secretariat and records.
2. He wrote the Sangita Ratnakara.
3. The style credited to him uses black basalt laid without mortar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Hemadri was Shrikaranadhipa under Mahadeva and Ramachandra, and Hemadpanti style uses basalt with no mortar; the Sangita Ratnakara is Sarngadeva's.

s: The importance of Devagiri in the expansion of the Delhi Sultanate lay in the fact that it
o: was the first southern kingdom to fall to Delhi and opened routes towards major southern kingdoms
prevented all further Delhi campaigns into the Deccan
was the first capital established by the Hoysalas in northern India
served as the original capital of the Kakatiyas
x: Devagiri was the first southern kingdom to fall to Delhi, opening the road to Warangal, Dwarasamudra and Madurai.

s: In which year did the first Muslim invasion of the South, in which Alauddin Khalji defeated Ramachandra, take place?
x: In 1296 Alauddin Khalji defeated Ramachandra; the Yadavas became vassals and promised the Ellichpur revenue yearly.

s: After the 1296 raid, the yearly revenue of which place did the Yadavas promise to Alauddin Khalji?
x: Ramachandra promised the revenue of Ellichpur every year but did not send it.

s: Which of the following pairs (Delhi Sultanate and the Yadavas) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Raid of 1296 – Alauddin Khalji, acting for Sultan Jalaluddin
Malik Kafur's campaign of 1307-08 – submission of Harapaladeva
Mubarak Khalji's invasion of 1317-18 – Harapaladeva killed
Charge of conquered Andhra after 1323 – Malik Burhanuddin
x: In 1307-08 it was Ramachandra who submitted and was taken to Delhi; Harapaladeva was killed in Mubarak Khalji's invasion of 1317-18.
